items.followUp: Name the five kingdoms and give one characteristic of each kingdom.

rubric.why: Monera includes organisms with prokaryotic cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Monera and giving a correct characteristic such as having prokaryotic cells.

rubric.why: Protista consists mainly of simple, mostly unicellular eukaryotes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Protista and stating that its organisms are eukaryotic.

rubric.why: Fungi are eukaryotic heterotrophs that obtain nutrients by absorption.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Fungi and giving a correct characteristic such as heterotrophic nutrition.

rubric.why: Plants are multicellular eukaryotes that generally make their own food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Plantae and stating that its organisms are generally autotrophic.

rubric.why: Animal cells do not have cell walls.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Animalia and giving a correct characteristic such as having no cell walls.

modelAnswer: The five-kingdom system proposed by R. H. Whittaker classifies organisms using features such as cell type, body organisation and mode of nutrition.
Monera: prokaryotic, usually unicellular organisms, such as bacteria.
Protista: eukaryotic organisms, mostly unicellular, such as Amoeba.
Fungi: eukaryotic heterotrophs that absorb nutrients; their cell walls generally contain chitin.
Plantae: multicellular eukaryotes that are generally autotrophic, make food by photosynthesis and have cellulose cell walls.
Animalia: multicellular eukaryotes that obtain food by ingestion and have no cell walls.

items.followUp: Describe the roles of ATP and NADPH produced during the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Light absorbed by chlorophyll supplies energy for the light reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chlorophyll absorbs light energy.

rubric.why: Water is split, releasing oxygen, hydrogen ions and electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing photolysis of water and identifying oxygen as a product.

rubric.why: Electron transport provides energy for ATP formation by photophosphorylation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that ATP is formed using energy from electron transport.

rubric.why: NADP accepts electrons and hydrogen ions and is reduced to NADPH.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that NADP is reduced to NADPH.

modelAnswer: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy and its electrons become excited.
Water molecules split by photolysis into hydrogen ions, electrons and oxygen; oxygen is released.
Excited electrons pass along an electron transport chain, and their energy is used to make ATP by photophosphorylation.
NADP accepts electrons and hydrogen ions and is reduced to NADPH.

items.followUp: Explain anaemia and haemophilia, and state how each affects the blood.

rubric.why: Anaemia involves too few red blood cells or insufficient haemoglobin, reducing oxygen transport.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing anaemia as a deficiency of red blood cells or haemoglobin and linking it to reduced oxygen-carrying capacity.

rubric.why: Haemophilia is an inherited disorder in which blood does not clot normally.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying haemophilia as an inherited blood-clotting disorder that can cause prolonged bleeding.

rubric.why: Leukaemia is a cancer involving abnormal production of white blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing leukaemia as cancer or abnormal uncontrolled production of white blood cells.

rubric.why: Thalassaemia is an inherited disorder affecting haemoglobin production and can cause anaemia.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking thalassaemia to abnormal haemoglobin production.

modelAnswer: Anaemia: a condition in which the blood has too few red blood cells or too little haemoglobin, reducing its oxygen-carrying capacity.
Haemophilia: an inherited disorder in which blood clotting is impaired, so bleeding may continue for a long time.
Leukaemia: a cancer of blood-forming tissues that causes abnormal, uncontrolled production of white blood cells and interferes with normal blood-cell production.
Thalassaemia: an inherited disorder in which haemoglobin is made abnormally; it can cause fragile red blood cells and anaemia.

items.followUp: Define physiology and state how it differs from anatomy.

rubric.why: Anatomy is a branch of biology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying anatomy as a branch of biology.

rubric.why: Anatomy studies the internal structure of organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that anatomy studies the internal structure of organisms.

modelAnswer: Anatomy is the branch of biology that studies the internal structure of organisms.

items.followUp: State two important contributions of Ibn al-Haytham to scientific study.

rubric.why: Jabir Bin Hayan is credited with introducing experimental research in science.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that he introduced or promoted experimental methods in science.

rubric.why: His writings included books on plants and animals, and he is widely known as the father of chemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning his books on plants and animals or identifying him as the father of chemistry.

modelAnswer: Jabir Bin Hayan introduced experimental methods in scientific research.
He wrote books on plants and animals and is known as the father of chemistry.
